title: LiteRT delegate compatibility matrix snapshot
description: One snapshot file per (backend x litert_version). Never merge backends or runtime versions into one file. Every verdict derived from this file must carry the file's backend and litert_version. Known native backend ID candidates (final registry pending owner confirmation): gpu_mldrift (Android ML Drift / OpenCL), webgpu_mac (Mac/desktop WebGPU), metal_mldrift (iOS Metal), cpu_xnnpack, gpu_v3dv (Pi 5). REGISTERED browser backend IDs (schema 1.1, Phase 6): wasm_xnnpack (LiteRT.js WASM CPU/XNNPACK), webgpu_mldrift (LiteRT.js WebGPU / ML Drift), webnn (LiteRT.js WebNN, experimental) — for browser backends the version axis carried in litert_version is the @litertjs/core version. Registration adds NO entries: op-level web entries are never derived from model-level sweep results (the trap rule); browser snapshots stay empty — and the linter honestly reports `unknown` — until a runtime log names a specific op, captured as evidence. Schema 1.2 (Phase 10, additive): rewrite_hints entries may carry a transform_id linking the prose hint to an executable edge-fix transform rule (transform_rule.schema.json). REGISTERED NPU backend IDs (schema 1.3, Phase 13 — candidates pending owner confirmation of the device fleet): npu_qnn (Qualcomm Hexagon via QNN), npu_neuropilot (MediaTek NeuroPilot). The same registration discipline as Phase 6: zero entries added — op-level NPU entries require a runtime log naming the specific op (captured as evidence) or an npu_adb probe result; the trap rule applies to device-run results in both lanes. NPU behavior varies per SoC and vendor SDK, so `target` (device, soc, driver — driver carries the vendor SDK version) is MANDATORY on NPU snapshots, enforced by semantic lint in `matrix validate`.

schema_version.description: 1.1 (Phase 6, additive): browser backend IDs registered in the top-level description; no structural change. 1.2 (Phase 10, additive): optional rewrite_hints[].transform_id. 1.3 (Phase 13, additive): NPU backend IDs registered in the top-level description; mandatory `target` on NPU snapshots via semantic lint; no structural change. Older documents remain valid.

litert_version.description: The LiteRT runtime version this snapshot describes. Delegate op support changes across versions; snapshots are carried forward explicitly, never edited in place. For browser backends (wasm_xnnpack, webgpu_mldrift, webnn) this is the @litertjs/core version — the same version-axis rule, web edition.

backend.description: Delegate/backend ID this snapshot describes. Kept as a pattern-constrained string in schema 1.0; the ID registry is documented in this schema's top-level description until the owner confirms the final set.

op.description: Exact TFLite builtin operator name (e.g. FULLY_CONNECTED, GATHER_ND, TRANSPOSE_CONV). No aliases, no prettified names.

dtypes.description: Tensor dtypes this entry covers. Absent or empty means the entry is op-generic (matches any dtype at lower lookup precedence).

constraints.description: Shape/attribute constraints under which this entry applies. Keys max_rank/min_rank compare numerically against shape_meta rank at lookup; other keys match by equality.

status.description: incorrect = the delegate compiles and executes the op but produces numerics outside tolerance vs the CPU reference.

transform_id.description: Optional (schema 1.2) link from this prose hint to the executable edge-fix transform rule with the same id (transform_rule.schema.json).

provenance.description: measured entries additionally require evidence.source_model, evidence.litert_version, and evidence.date (enforced by semantic lint in `matrix validate`).

derived_from.description: Present when this entry was carried forward from an earlier snapshot without re-measurement; pins the source snapshot's litert_version and generated_at.
